milestones.title: Revisited with the partner's samples at the acceptance trial (45.2-12); a mail adapter is planned if a partner hands over labelled messages as files

remediation: NATO profiles labelled mail (ADatP-4778.2 chapter 3, a binding object in a mail header beside the RFC 7444 security label header) and labelled chat (chapter 4, XMPP), and military mail gateways support them with S/MIME security labels. Your organization's exchange is a file handover at the release boundary, not a mail or chat gateway, so these labels are not read: a saved message arrives as a plain file and is held as unlabelled unless a marking your organization lists is found in it. A mail adapter is planned when a partner or the allied test cell shows it hands over labelled messages as files. Source: .planning/phases/45.2-nato-and-five-eyes-exchange-part-2-ztdf-and-the-nato-texts/45.2-CONTEXT.md D-33 and 45.2-RESEARCH.md section 12.3.
title: Labelled mail and chat from partners are not read
